title: How does the farthest XY compare with the diagonals AC and BD?
description: The farthest position of the points X and Y is placed at opposite corners and compared with the two diagonals AC and BD of the rectangle. Keeko's doubt is that the farthest distance is the long side of the rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: when X and Y sit at opposite corners, the line XY is a diagonal, so the farthest XY equals AC or BD. Watch for students who think the longest line in a rectangle is its long side.

source: How does the farthest distance between X and Y compare with
video_script.why: A learner compares the farthest length of XY with the two diagonals of the rectangle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with AB seven centimetres and BC four centimetres, and its diagonals AC and BD
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with its two diagonals AC and BD, and the points X and Y moving to opposite corners
video_script.wrong_answer: the farthest distance is the long side of the rectangle
video_script.wrong_move: takes the long side AB as the greatest length in the rectangle and ignores the slanting lines between opposite corners
video_script.payoff_line: The farthest ex why is equal to a diagonal.

final_answer.value: The farthest XY equals AC or BD, about 8 cm 1 mm

maths_rules: XY is farthest when X and Y are at opposite corners
X at A and Y at C gives XY = AC; X at D and Y at B gives XY = DB
AC = BD = square root of (7 times 7 plus 4 times 4) = square root of 65, about 8.06 cm, about 8 cm 1 mm
the long side AB = 7 cm is shorter than the diagonal
video_script.design: The points are sent to opposite corners twice, and the line XY is laid over each diagonal.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the farthest distance is the long side of the rectangle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the long side is only seven centimetres, and that is the shortest ex why.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>A diagonal goes across and also up, so it is longer than any side.
